carries.draft: Focusing (Eugene Gendlin's method of listening to a vague, felt sense in your body) can especially help you notice feelings and preferences the part you've been playing learned to overlook.
carries.guide: Focusing can be especially useful for noticing feelings and preferences the conditioned self learned to overlook;

carries.draft: Any words you put to them can stay tentative ("I hate cooking... or just for everybody?") while you look at what they seem to mean and revise how you read them.
carries.guide: you can then put tentative words to them, examine what they seem to mean, and revise your interpretation.

carries.draft: Some people also benefit from temporary, intentional distance from whoever they've been playing the part for, long enough for conditioning to quiet down and real preferences to surface.
carries.guide: Some people also benefit from temporary, intentional distance long enough for the conditioning to quiet down and authentic preferences to surface.
